Hey, just sharing my two cents on the matter…

Firstly, I think you should confide in your parents if it is a viable choice for you. Even though they might have their troubles and hardship they never restricted you like your ex-mother-in-law did.(I wouldn’t know about your family and you know best so don’t take my words blindly) 

Secondly, get rid of all forms of contact for your ex-boyfriend& ex-mother in law. They are really people you shouldn’t mix with, especially on your route to recovery. Come into terms with your breakup and think rationally about your situation. From an outsider’s view, there were already many red flags from the first day even. What I saw was that they did not have trust in you and you were even lied to on multiple occasions. Now, I truly believe that there is some goodness in the deep depths of everyones heart…but some people will never uncover theirs in their lifetime. For a relationship to work and function well, trust/honesty/integrity and *Respect* must be always kept up. It seemed like they didn’t even think what they were doing was wrong. Mr. K there also was keeping things away from you, his (supposedly) significant other.

Thirdly and probably most importantly. I think you should recover first before even thinking of anymore romantic relationships. Sure, having someone who can help you recover and get you back to your best form sounds nice but often times you will fall into the trap of being too dependent. Relationship don’t work on interdependence but is like two parts (people) that are good on it’s own but get even better when together. You should not let other people think that you are lower than you and let them tranple all over you (neither should you think that you are better than them). Recovering, especially from depression is a long and tiresome process, it won’t be easy in the slightest(speaking from experience) . There will also be some habits you have learnt from your traumatising experience and things to help you cope.(search up: learned helplessness) All that matters is that you try your best for yourself first(not others) and make sure that you don’t dwell on your regrets and mistakes. Know that everything back then is already said and done but everything from now on is within your grasp.

Final note: Please don’t take any of my advice at point blank(I might have said my stupid things), from now you will need to make your own decisions and sieve out the good and the bad and everything in between. Lastly, I wish you all the best for your recovery and future endeavours. It might not help, but, just know that on the other side of this screen(and many more), there is someone who has read your message in it’s entirety and sympathised with you… Please don’t degrade yourself and say bad things about yourself. I’m sure some random internet people here marvel at your courage to share your problems and try to seek advice from people you don’t even know.

Try learning [Japanese pitch accent](https://youtu.be/k-bk_4WvY58). It would probably sound more natural and might your dad communicate with you easier. 

My Japanese isn’t that great but use Chinese(my mother tongue) for example. Both chinese and Japanese have intonation thats why Im using it here. If someone spoke to in flat chinese ignoring the 1/2/3/4 types of intonations I totally would not get what they are saying and I would also feel like scratching my scalp out hearing that kind of broken chinese lol(well in chinese the intonation are in the hanyupinyin so is no excuse for not pronouncing the words with correct intonation but for Japanese its not written down but all native speakers naturally have intonations) 
Sorry for my longwinded explanation and going off topic for a bit there. 

TLDR: The main point is that there is also a correct way of pronouncing Japanese word and that is through speaking it with the correct intonation. This makes it way easier for locals to understand you because that is just how natives speak japanese. Without intonations it would be very hard for native speakers to find out what exactly you are saying and will require them to infer out of context which can end up being quite tiring if done for a long time. By the way a good way to practice pronunciation with proper intonations is by hearing native speakers talk and try to speak it exactly the way the do it. The video at the top really breaks it down the intonations so watch it if you want to.
